correctness.rationale: For all integers k>=2, any leaf vector has least deviation from its mean at most floor(k/2)/k, by comparing the lower and upper leaf-group averages. A balanced binary leaf configuration attains the bound exactly, including equality under the strict test. Its frozen leaves produce iid Bernoulli hub forcing; interval-covering affine contractions with 0<rho<=1/2 and repeated finite words prove almost-sure full interval accumulation. Disjoint-block word-frequency strong laws establish weak empirical-measure convergence when rho=1/2; exact dyadic cylinder masses, entropy typical sets and non-atomicity yield Hausdorff dimension and parity classification. The finite rational checker passed 19,525 grid profiles, canonical frozen shells, exact transition recurrences, dyadic cylinder checks, and stationary mean/variance identities; infinite claims rest on proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper defines the oriented-neighborhood model and reports finite dynamic examples, but its inspected model and results do not give the sharp star freezing extremal bound or the resulting almost-sure full-interval and parity-dependent occupation laws. Standard Deffuant convergence and mean-field results require symmetric dyadic reception, failing for this one-sided star. The biased binary entropy theorem is known; its application alone does not settle the exact NDW freeze threshold. Searches of accessible historical claims and published index results found no same-claim or stronger implication. Residual risk remains for unindexed specialist papers; originality is best-knowledge, not guaranteed uniqueness.

value.rationale: A mathematically natural social-network boundary becomes exact for all star degrees and every real confidence bound, including the strict-threshold equality case. The sharp obstruction separates fixed but isolated leaves from a dynamically wandering, never-settling hub; the same model at half compromise gives a population-parity transition between uniform Lebesgue occupation and singular full-support occupation. This exact warning applies to interpreting finite simulations of asymmetric neighborhood opinion dynamics and is not a routine restatement of an existing convergence result.
